summary: AMASS Phase 6E — Legacy → Property Identity migration backend verified end-to-end. 16/16 pytest cases pass covering AuthZ, /migrate-legacy/status counts, dry_run (no writes), real migration (properties_geo + property_listings + property_representations + audit rows + legacy flag), idempotency, missing-GPS skip handling, post-migration passport + properties-v2 endpoints, and v1 /api/properties regression. Test seeds fresh legacy docs directly in MongoDB (since the previously seeded 10 were already migrated in an earlier session) with proper cleanup afterwards.

minor.issue: run_migration query is `{migrated_to_amass_property_id: {$exists: false}}` — this means legacy docs with missing lat/lng are NEVER stamped with the flag, so they get re-scanned on every subsequent run (returned as `status='skipped_missing_gps'`). Not strictly a bug (no duplicates are created) but the review request wording 'Second run scans 0 unmigrated docs' will always be false as long as any missing-GPS legacy doc exists. Consider either stamping missing-GPS docs with `migration_skipped_at`/`skip_reason` so they drop out of the query, or documenting this behaviour.

For legacy docs where `agent_id` is missing/null, NO property_representations doc is created (the block is guarded by `if legacy.get('agent_id')`). All seeded legacy docs in prod have agent_id, but the review requirement '(d) property_representations doc created (APPROVED if listing_source==mandated, else PENDING)' does not explicitly allow this bypass. If a mandated/owner_listed legacy row without agent_id ever appears, it will silently skip rep creation.

DEFAULT_VISIBILITY_MIGRATED sets `show_photos, show_current_listings, show_representatives, show_history, show_amenities, show_physical_details, show_size, allow_enquiries, show_qr = True` for every migrated property regardless of legacy state. Legacy `verified=false` / `status='pending'` properties will therefore have their full passport publicly visible after migration — worth confirming this matches the intended policy.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Stamp missing-GPS legacy docs with a persistent skip marker so /status.pending drops to 0 and re-runs return total_scanned=0 (as the spec wording implies).
OPTIONAL: Consider whether property_representations must be created even when legacy.agent_id is null (currently silently skipped).
OPTIONAL: Review whether migrated legacy properties should default to ALL passport-visibility flags = True (privacy vs continuity trade-off).
critical_code_review_comments: migrate_one guards insertion with `if legacy.get('agent_id')` for property_representations — silently drops the row when agent_id is falsy. Consider explicit logging + a report entry so admins see it.
run_migration's outer try/except around migrate_one swallows tracebacks (only captures str(e)). Fine for a batch job but a logger.exception would help ops.
migrate_one uses `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` per call — fine but the same `now` is not shared with listing/rep created_at when `legacy.created_at` is missing → tiny ordering skew; not a bug.
STATE_CODES uses fixed 3-letter codes; unknown states fall back to first-3-uppercase which could collide (e.g. 'Kwara'→'KWA' vs. 'Kwa Ibom'). Low risk given the current corpus.

The migration endpoint has NO write-lock — two concurrent admin clicks would each try to migrate the same pending doc. Duplicate creation is prevented only by the `migrated_to_amass_property_id: {$exists: False}` filter being re-evaluated inside migrate_one, but property_id_counters is atomic so at worst two AMASS IDs would be burned. Consider a coarse-grained lock or a 'currently_running' flag.
seed_data_creation: Test seeds 4 fresh legacy docs directly into MongoDB inside a module-scoped fixture (1 verified+mandated, 1 verified+owner_listed, 1 unverified pending, 1 missing-GPS). Cleanup fixture removes them plus their derived properties_geo / property_listings / property_representations / property_audit_logs rows after the module finishes. Seed docs are tagged with `_test_tag` for identification.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test MUST be run without pytest-xdist because the module-scoped `seeded_legacy` fixture is shared across TestStatus / TestDryRun / TestRealMigration / TestIdempotency / TestPostMigrationEndpoints / TestLegacyRegression and the DryRun assertion compares Mongo counters before/after the call — parallel workers cause interleaving that breaks the invariant. Invoke with: `pytest backend/tests/test_phase6e_migrate_legacy.py -o addopts= -v`. Sets EXPO_BACKEND_URL default to the preview host; override via env if needed.
rca_of_issue: Initial run under the project's default `-n auto --dist loadscope` (in pytest.ini) caused 3 flaky failures because TestStatus / TestDryRun / TestIdempotency ran concurrently with TestRealMigration on the same seeded legacy docs — status counts drifted mid-test and DryRun's before/after DB counters overlapped with the real migration writes in another worker. Also, Idempotency's `total_scanned==0` assertion was too strict: missing-GPS legacy docs are never stamped with `migrated_to_amass_property_id`, so they re-appear in `run_migration`'s scan cursor forever. Fixes: (1) added `-o addopts=` instructions + doc header to force serial execution; (2) relaxed Idempotency check to `migrated == 0` and DB counters unchanged (which is what 'no duplicates' actually means).
